The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Summary of 2024 Electoral Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive plan for national renewal focused on economic stability, improved public services, and constitutional reform.

## Economic Framework

The document establishes strict fiscal rules requiring day-to-day costs to be met by revenues and debt to fall as a share of the economy by the fifth year of forecasts. Central to the economic plan is an industrial strategy featuring a statutory Industrial Strategy Council, a National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion, and planning reform to deliver 1.5 million new homes.

The approach emphasises partnership between government, business, and trade unions. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a fairer system, reforming workplace pensions, maintaining corporation tax at 25%, and establishing Skills England to coordinate workforce development.

## Energy and Environment

A central commitment involves achieving clean power by 2030 through a new publicly-owned energy company headquartered in Scotland. The plan includes doubling onshore wind, tripling solar power, and quadrupling offshore wind. The manifesto proposes investing £8.3 billion in this company while also committing £6.6 billion for home energy efficiency upgrades.

Environmental measures include stricter water company regulation, creation of new national river walks and forests, and stronger animal welfare protections.

## Public Services

Healthcare reforms focus on reducing NHS waiting times through 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and reforming dentistry with 700,000 additional urgent appointments. The manifesto commits to developing a National Care Service with uniform standards.

Education proposals include recruiting 6,500 new teachers, establishing 3,000 nurseries in primary schools, providing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, and creating specialist Technical Excellence Colleges.

## Security and Justice

Defence commitments include maintaining nuclear deterrent, upholding the commitment to the transatlantic alliance, conducting a Strategic Defence Review, and continuing support for Ukraine. Border security measures propose establishing a new Border Security Command with counter-terrorism powers and hiring additional caseworkers to clear asylum backlogs.

Criminal justice reforms emphasise neighbourhood policing with thousands of new officers, halving knife crime within a decade, and establishing specialist units in every police force for serious sexual offences.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed changes include establishing an Ethics and Integrity Commission, removing hereditary peers from the upper legislative chamber, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for that chamber, and extending voting rights to 16-17 year-olds. The manifesto commits to strengthening devolution through a new Council of Nations and Regions and improved intergovernmental cooperation.

## Employment and Equality

Worker protections include banning exploitative zero-hour contracts, ending fire-and-rehire practices, establishing day-one employment rights, and creating a Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care. The manifesto proposes a Race Equality Act and measures to reduce gender, disability, and ethnicity pay gaps.

## International Relations

Foreign policy priorities include resetting European relationships while remaining outside the single market and customs union, seeking new trade agreements aligned with industrial strategy, pursuing climate leadership through a Clean Power Alliance, and restoring international development spending to 0.7% of gross national income when fiscal circumstances allow.

# Summary of the 2024 Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive policy platform addressing interconnected crises in cost of living, public services, and climate change. The document argues that the UK, despite being a wealthy nation, faces severe challenges including healthcare waiting lists, housing shortages, and environmental degradation.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The manifesto proposes significant NHS investment, estimating £28 billion annually by 2030 for England, plus £20 billion in capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, ensuring universal NHS dentistry access, and boosting staff pay. The document opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, it proposes £20 billion annual investment to introduce free personal care, establish career structures for care workers, and address the 400,000-person backlog awaiting care services.

## Housing

The manifesto calls for 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29 billion over five years in home insulation retrofits. It emphasises building genuinely affordable homes with proper infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate

Central proposals include achieving approximately 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, ending new fossil fuel extraction licences, eliminating oil and gas subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. The manifesto opposes nuclear power development and supports community ownership of energy infrastructure.

## Economy and Work

The document proposes £40 billion annual green investment, bringing privatised utilities (railways, water, energy companies) into public ownership, and establishing regional mutual banks. Worker-focused policies include a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and moving toward a four-day working week.

## Taxation and Public Finance

Revenue proposals include wealth taxes on assets above £10 million, aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, reforming inheritance tax, and introducing carbon taxes. The manifesto estimates raising £50-70 billion annually through tax reforms, primarily affecting the wealthiest.

## Welfare and Poverty

Commitments include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, ending the five-week benefits wait, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, increasing disability benefits by 5%, and working toward Universal Basic Income.

## Education

Proposals cover £8 billion school investment, £2.5 billion annually for building repairs, £5 billion for special needs provision, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and investing in early years and further education.

## Transport

The manifesto proposes £10 billion annual public transport subsidies, railway renationalisation, £2.5 billion annually for cycling and walking infrastructure, free bus travel for under-18s, ending new road building, and banning petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027.

## Environment and Nature

Key commitments include creating a Rights of Nature Act giving nature legal personhood, protecting 30% of land and sea by 2030, returning water companies to public ownership, strengthening pollution enforcement, and introducing new Right to Roam legislation.

## Democracy and Rights

Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post voting with proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber replacing the current upper house, defending human rights legislation, and supporting national self-determination for constituent UK nations.

## Immigration

The manifesto advocates ending hostile environment policies, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing, ending immigration detention except for public safety reasons, and removing minimum income requirements for family visas.

## International Affairs

Foreign policy priorities include supporting an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognising Palestinian statehood, ending arms exports to Israel, continuing Ukraine support, increasing overseas aid to 1% of national income, working toward EU membership, and supporting nuclear disarmament including cancelling the current nuclear weapons programme.

The manifesto presents these proposals as interconnected solutions, arguing that addressing climate change simultaneously resolves cost-of-living pressures and inequality through warmer homes, cheaper energy, stronger public services, and restored natural environments.
